subject: MedicClear DPA: attestation & operational evidence for no-training and residency
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@mediclear.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mediclear.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Initial DPA questions — no-training and residency attestation

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this on. Procurement asked me to surface a couple of hard requirements from our legal and security teams before we progress to signature:

- A clear, contract-level no-training ("no learn") commitment for our tenant data, with explicit carve-outs (if any) called out.
- Evidence you can provide that all processing for our EU tenant will be resident in the EU (or an onshore alternative) and how you handle key custody (KMS).
- A subprocessor inventory and whether Redwood provides attestation (signed statement) from subprocessors about non-use for model improvement.

Can you share a redlined DPA and an operational evidence pack for these items? If you can point to an existing SOC2 or cert that covers the control set, that helps speed review.

Our timeline is tight — procurement would like this wrapped by the end of next week (23 Feb).

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Legal Ops, MedicClear Health
elena.rossi@mediclear.com

Attachment: MedicClear_requirements_20260215.docx (attachment stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@mediclear.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions — no-training and residency attestation

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. I'll coordinate internally and get a redline + evidence pack over by EOD Monday. Quick answers inline:

- No-training: Redwood can include a dedicated no-training clause for MedicClear that prohibits using tenant content to improve public or private models. We also document operational controls (ephemeral KV, tenant isolation) in the evidence pack.
- Residency & KMS: We offer EU residency for customer processing and can support onshore KMS (bring-your-own-key or Redwood-managed keys with EU KMS).
- Subprocessor attestations: We can provide our current subprocessor inventory and copies of attestation letters where subprocessors have signed standard non-use language. For subprocessors that do not provide attestations we will provide compensating controls.

Cc'ing Kimberly (legal) for suggested contract language and David (ops) for the evidence artifacts.

Next steps: Kimberly will draft a suggested clause and David will attach the operational evidence pack (SOC2 excerpt, subprocessor inventory, KMS residency note). After you review we can circulate a DocuSign-ready DPA.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Attachments: none

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@mediclear.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mediclear.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA questions — no-training and residency attestation

Jordan — thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifying points from legal/security:

1) The no-training clause must cover internal model improvement and all 3rd-party model providers engaged by Redwood. We need a sample contract sentence we can paste into our master DPA.
2) For subprocessors, procurement wants to see (a) the current inventory, (b) a timeline for notification of new subprocessors, and (c) template attestation language from subprocessors.
3) For evidence we prefer a hashed export or SFTP export option (not just API) for forensic transfer if needed.

If you can provide the redline + the operational pack that addresses the above, procurement will review and circle back with minor edits.

Elena

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 13:30:00 +0000
Subject: Draft language + evidence list for MedicClear DPA

Elena —

Thanks for the detailed asks. Attached are two items: (1) a redline DPA with suggested no-training and subprocessor notification clauses, and (2) an "operational evidence pack" zip with SOC2 excerpt pages, current subprocessor inventory, KMS residency statement, and our template subprocessor attestation. Highlights below.

Draft no-training clause (suggested):
"Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, improve, or adapt its models or any third-party models or services for any purpose other than providing the Services to Customer, except with Customer's prior written consent. Redwood shall ensure that any Subprocessor that has access to Customer Data is bound by contractual obligations to prohibit the use of Customer Data for model training or improvement."

Subprocessor controls:
- Current inventory attached (CSV).
- We notify customers of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding; emergency critical subprocessors will be communicated within 5 business days with a mitigation plan.
- Attestation: attached template which most subprocessors sign; where we cannot obtain a signature we provide compensating controls and a remediation timeline.

Residency & KMS:
- All EU-region processing and KMS options are documented in the evidence pack (we support Redwood-managed EU KMS and BYOK with EU key material).

Attachments included: MedicClear_DPA_Redwood_redlines_20260215.pdf; operational_evidence_pack_20260215.zip

If that language looks good to you, Jordan will circulate the DocuSign packet and we can accept minor procurement edits. If you need an explicit "third-party attestation" from a subprocessor we can surface the signed letters we have on file, but for a small set of subprocessors we may only provide signed remediation commitments.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 07:55:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft language + evidence list for MedicClear DPA

Kimberly — the redline and pack arrived, thank you. A few follow-ups from legal and security after an initial pass:

- The draft no-training sentence is close. Legal would like the parenthetical that lists "including but not limited to model providers, third-party training services, and research partners" to make it explicit.
- Security wants the SFTP export workflow documented in the pack (hashing + retention policy) — currently the pack covers API export but not SFTP specifics.
- Procurement requests DocuSign-ready DPA and a single PDF with signed subprocessor attestations where available. If you can provide an expected timeline to get signed attestations for the three subprocessors flagged in the inventory (logging provider, metrics/CDN, and a small analytics vendor), that would be helpful.

If you can update those three items and push the DocuSign link, we'll aim to complete legal review by Monday and move to signature the same week.

Elena
